source: App Store Reviews/7. Habit Tracker - HabitKit - Streaks & Accountability/reviews.jsonl
text:
I really love how simple and easy this app is to use. The pricing is also extremely reasonable for $0.99 when most apps charge way more just for some basic functions. I think it would be great if we would were able to create our own account so we can sync progress across different devices. 

I have ADHD and this app really helps me stay motivated and manage my executive dysfunction because I have to gamify EVERYTHING just to do simple things. I like how we are able to select different days for when we want to track a habit, but I wish we could select different reminder times for different days as well under the same habit. Say you want to add a yoga habit for each day, but want reminders at 2:00pm on certain days and 3:00pm on other days for those with varying schedules.

 I also think sub-habit/task would be an interesting game changer. Say you’re trying to incorporate an entire morning routine habit, you can just label the habit morning routine, and you can click it to open, add a sub-habit/task, like make bed, brush teeth, do skin care, and once you check off all three of those things, it will complete that habit for the day. I feel like this would help with lessening the amount of habits you have to make when one habit can incorporate many things you want to do!

source: App Store Reviews/9. Dear Me - Daily Routine Tracker - Self Care & ADHD Habit Planner/reviews.jsonl
text:
Depuis que j’utilise cette appli je suis vraiment plus productive et je pense à tout (chose qui n’est pas aisé quand on a une mémoire à court terme). 

Cependant, il y a 2 améliorations qui me semblent indispensables pour avoir une utilisation optimale :
- classer la liste des tâches du jour par fréquence (quotidien, semaine, mensuel). Quand on a trop de tâches, ça devient difficilement gérable car tout est mélangé. 
- si la tâche est à la semaine ou mensuelle (peu importe le nombre de fois), que la tâche s’efface sur les jours restants une fois que l’objectif a été atteint. Ça reste compliqué sur 30 jours d’anticiper 1 tâche sur 1 jour en particulier (surtout que les jours ne sont pas notés quand on sélectionne la date). 

Si cela est actuellement possible, je n’ai pas trouvé comment le configurer. À part ça, l’appli reste très utile.

source: App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
text:
In a way, it is the best habit-tracking app.

However, one feature drives me mad: you cannot simply mark a habit as done; instead, you are forced to start a timer and complete an entire block in one go.

Give me the ability to turn off the timer and use it as a ‘to-do’ list, and you’ll earn 5 stars from me.

The timing aspect makes things feel rushed. I understand why some people would want it, but making it optional would significantly increase my satisfaction with this app!

Can be as low pressure as you want it to be. There are certainly many other uses I haven't tried.

text: I have been using this app for over a year now just about everyday. I struggle with executive dysfunction and time blindness. This app has helped me go from someone who is always late to someone who is always on time. This app has allowed me to get ready in the mornings when it seems impossible. source: App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
text: This app is amazing. I’m an ADHD mom with three kids under 5. Due to my husband’s work schedule, I’m usually alone in the mornings trying to get my three kids out the door and to preschool/daycare before I head to work. Mornings were HORRIBLE. We were running late every morning, no matter what I did. It was not uncommon for me to leave the house in tears. This app has definitely helped keep me on track and also helped me identify which tasks were taking too long in the morning. Additionally, I made a nighttime routine that helps me stay focused, as I often go to bed ridiculously late. I’ve tried so many productivity apps but this is a keeper. If mornings are a nightmare or you struggle to go to bed at a reasonable time, get this app!! I will never go back!

source: App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
text: I’m finding it hard to grapple with these timer based apps that try to direct me. I wasn’t to complete things in my own time but need checklists to keep myself on track. I understand the philosophy of routines that build habits like this but I need to also be able to check things off my todo list without starting a timer and going through things in sequence. I need more flexibility. A dumb mode where I can just check off what I’ve already done and look over what’s left etc very quickly. I’m not a robot I do things at different times, for different durations and in different orders but I still need something to keep me on track with daily repeating todos and reminders. I find myself wrestling with this app. Would work if I could just add tasks without durations and complete them without starting the timer.

source: App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
text:
I just got this app and am setting up my morning routine. I can see how much it would help me with my ADHD/time blindness! The only problem is there are no instructions or tutorials. I’ve read reviews of people talking about things they’re doing with this app. I only wish I knew how to do them. There's urprisingly nothing useable on YouTube! It’s very odd because clearly they put in a ton of clinical research and show a great understanding of ADHD core problems. 

Is there a way to search all of the included habits? No idea but I hope so. For now I’m just finding things randomly in the limited categories (morning, night, Oprah Winfrey, Healthy) which are incomplete at best. So I'm sure there must be another way.

I'd like to set a morning routine that includes everyday tasks that I can add certain chores to on different days. Again, I'm sure you can do this but there's no way to find out.

I got a month of premium membership but again, I didn't get any information on how to use it. TBH I'm not even sure what it includes.  I figured for $2.99 I'd have time to see if it was worth it.

Overall, I see a lot of potential but I'll have to add "Try to figure out how to use this app, 30 minutes" as a habit if I want to really benefit, which is the opposite of what a person with ADHD needs. In fact, I'm getting overwhelmed just thinking abouthow many steps there will be to finish this one routine without knowing the right way to do it.

source: App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
text: Excellent for ADHD, time blindness and procrastination. I tend to make a list, do 1 or 2 out of 10 things, sit on the couch and then feel awful about myself later on. This app gives you a full customized visual schedule, audio reminders and a visual timer so that you are 100% on top of your day. The timer is really the life changing aspect, I put every single task in this app (eat, shower, etc) because as my fellow NDs know, you can procrastinate anything and everything for hours on end and not even notice the time.  I enjoy picking the little icons out and organizing my routine so it provides some enjoyment which motivates me to open the app in the mornings. Very user friendly. I also like how I can build in new things I want to incorporate into my routine such as exercise. If I see a new task and a timer, I am more likely to try the new task because I set designated time aside for it, rather than looking at the new task and scratching it off my list.

source: App Store Reviews/5. Routine Planner, Habit Tracker - Daily Time Management for ADHD/reviews.jsonl
text:
This app has been such a blessing to me! A lot of us that suffer from ADHD have time blindness. We have no true concept of how much time a task actually takes us. This app gives me the independence to make my own schedule but gives me the accountability I need to actually see how much time it really takes me to do things and how I can adjust. For example, I’ve been using it the most on work days. Before Routinery, I was chronically late 10-15 mins for work. In my head, my morning routine takes 30 minutes. After Routinery, I learned it actually takes me an hour and 5 minutes to get ready for the day and leave on time. 

My mornings used to be so scattered (even on medication) and now it’s smooth sailing. I can even make time to sit on my couch, catch up on the local news, and drink my coffee. 

Thank you for this wonderful app!
